title: 致醫界通函第 616 號：延長擴大公費流感抗病毒藥劑使用對象「有類流感症狀，且具下列身分之流感高傳播族群」之適用期限至 10 月 31 日
summary: 疾管署延長擴大公費流感抗病毒藥劑使用對象「有類流感症狀，且具 7 類流感高傳播族群身分者」之適用期限至 2026 年 10 月 31 日；經醫師評估符合者不需快篩即可開立，用藥後至 SMIS 回報。
bodyMarkdown:
一、本署自 2026 年 8 月 24 日起擴大公費流感抗病毒藥劑使用對象「有類流感症狀，且具下列身分之流感高傳播族群」，原訂至 9 月 30 日止；考量國內流感疫情已進入流行期且持續上升，適用期限延長至 **2026 年 10 月 31 日止**。
二、流感高傳播族群：（一）醫事單位之防疫相關人員（含具執業登記醫事人員及醫療院所非醫事人員）；（二）安養、長期照顧（服務）等機構之受照顧者及所屬工作人員；（三）幼兒園托育人員、托育機構專業人員及居家托育人員（保母）；（四）幼兒園、國小、國中、高中、高職、五專一至三年級學生；（五）與流感重症高風險族群同住者或其照顧者；（六）禽畜養殖等相關行業工作人員、動物園工作人員及動物防疫人員；（七）其他人口密集機構（如軍營等）易發生群聚之人員。
三、經醫師評估符合公費藥劑用藥條件者，**不需流感快篩即可開立公費藥劑**，以把握用藥時機；用藥後請儘速至「智慧防疫物資管理資訊系統（SMIS）」回報。
四、公費藥劑配置於各縣市衛生局規劃之全國約 4,000 家合約醫療機構，籲請醫師善用公費藥劑，共同防治流感。

（原型示意：本文為通函摘述，正式內容以疾管署官網原件為準。）

en.title: Letter to the Medical Community No. 616: eligibility for government-funded influenza antivirals for "people with influenza-like symptoms who belong to the following high-transmission groups" extended to 31 October
en.summary: Taiwan CDC has extended to 31 October 2026 the period during which people with influenza-like symptoms in the seven high-transmission groups are eligible for government-funded influenza antivirals; no rapid test is needed if a physician judges them eligible, and use should be reported in SMIS afterwards.
en.bodyMarkdown:
1. Since 24 August 2026, Taiwan CDC has expanded eligibility for government-funded influenza antivirals to "people with influenza-like symptoms who belong to the following high-transmission groups", originally until 30 September. As influenza activity in Taiwan has entered the epidemic period and continues to rise, the period is extended **to 31 October 2026**.

2. The high-transmission groups are: (1) staff of healthcare units involved in epidemic prevention (including registered medical personnel and non-medical staff of medical institutions); (2) people cared for in nursing, long-term care (service) and similar facilities, and their staff; (3) kindergarten childcare workers, professionals in childcare institutions and home-based childcare providers (nannies); (4) students from kindergarten, elementary school, junior high, senior high, vocational high school and years 1–3 of five-year junior college; (5) people who live with, or care for, people at high risk of severe influenza; (6) workers in poultry and livestock farming and related trades, zoo workers and animal disease control personnel; (7) people in other crowded institutions (such as military barracks) where clusters are likely.

3. For those a physician judges to meet the conditions for the government-funded antiviral, **the antiviral can be prescribed without a rapid influenza test**, to make the most of the treatment window; after use, please report promptly in the Smart Epidemic Prevention Supplies Management Information System (SMIS).

4. Government-funded antivirals are stocked at about 4,000 contracted medical institutions nationwide, arranged by the county and city health bureaus. Physicians are urged to make good use of them to help control influenza.

(Illustrative prototype: this text is a summary of the letter; the original on the Taiwan CDC website prevails.)
